title: Core
description: The kinds every type extends (the seven of the work, and system), the root links every link type extends, and the system tier.

types.title: Actor
types.description: Holds authority, owns work and is waited on: a person, a company, an agent. One of the seven kinds of the work; every type extends one of them or the system kind.

status.description: Where it stands: one of its statuses, an open one while it is unfinished. Kept in the item's row.

confidence.description: 0 to 1: how sure the author is that this is true. Kept in the item's row.

source.description: Where its facts came from: the source of the change that made it, or of its op. Kept in the item's row.

types.title: Aim
types.description: Why work exists: what serves points at, such as a goal or an area. One of the seven kinds of the work; every type extends one of them or the system kind.

status.description: Where it stands: one of its statuses, an open one while it is unfinished. Kept in the item's row.

owner.description: Id of the person or agent responsible. Kept in the item's row.

confidence.description: 0 to 1: how sure the author is that this is true. Kept in the item's row.

source.description: Where its facts came from: the source of the change that made it, or of its op. Kept in the item's row.

types.title: Work
types.description: Open until finished; it blocks and is blocked: a task, a project, an issue. One of the seven kinds of the work; every type extends one of them or the system kind.

status.description: Where it stands: one of its statuses, an open one while it is unfinished. Kept in the item's row.

owner.description: Id of the person or agent responsible. Kept in the item's row.

confidence.description: 0 to 1: how sure the author is that this is true. Kept in the item's row.

source.description: Where its facts came from: the source of the change that made it, or of its op. Kept in the item's row.

types.title: Question
types.description: Open until settled, by someone's word or by evidence: a decision, a hypothesis, an idea. One of the seven kinds of the work; every type extends one of them or the system kind.

status.description: Where it stands: one of its statuses, an open one while it is unfinished. Kept in the item's row.

owner.description: Id of the person or agent responsible. Kept in the item's row.

confidence.description: 0 to 1: how sure the author is that this is true. Kept in the item's row.

source.description: Where its facts came from: the source of the change that made it, or of its op. Kept in the item's row.

types.title: Record
types.description: Explains, and is replaced by a newer one: a note, a result, a procedure, a document. One of the seven kinds of the work; every type extends one of them or the system kind.

status.description: Where it stands: one of its statuses, an open one while it is unfinished. Kept in the item's row.

owner.description: Id of the person or agent responsible. Kept in the item's row.

confidence.description: 0 to 1: how sure the author is that this is true. Kept in the item's row.

source.description: Where its facts came from: the source of the change that made it, or of its op. Kept in the item's row.

types.title: Occurrence
types.description: Happens at a time, and can be a gate: an event, a meeting, a release. One of the seven kinds of the work; every type extends one of them or the system kind.

status.description: Where it stands: one of its statuses, an open one while it is unfinished. Kept in the item's row.

owner.description: Id of the person or agent responsible. Kept in the item's row.

confidence.description: 0 to 1: how sure the author is that this is true. Kept in the item's row.

source.description: Where its facts came from: the source of the change that made it, or of its op. Kept in the item's row.

types.title: Place
types.description: Exists somewhere, physical or not; work lives in it or uses it: a resource, a repository, a file. One of the seven kinds of the work; every type extends one of them or the system kind.

status.description: Where it stands: one of its statuses, an open one while it is unfinished. Kept in the item's row.

confidence.description: 0 to 1: how sure the author is that this is true. Kept in the item's row.

source.description: Where its facts came from: the source of the change that made it, or of its op. Kept in the item's row.

types.title: System
types.description: The app's own configuration, kept as items: views, styles, screens, runs, sources, notifications, automations. Views of the work leave it out unless asked. Only the kernel's packs declare types of it.

status.description: Where it stands: one of its statuses, an open one while it is unfinished. Kept in the item's row.

source.description: Where its facts came from: the source of the change that made it, or of its op. Kept in the item's row.

role.description: What they do, in a few words.

types.title: Company
types.description: An organisation: a business, client, vendor or institution.

types.title: Agent
types.description: A non-human actor with its own identity, such as an AI agent or an automation.

kind.description: What sort of agent, e.g. claude-code.

types.title: Goal
types.description: An outcome that projects and tasks serve.

measure.description: How you will know it is achieved.

types.title: Area
types.description: An ongoing responsibility with no end date.

types.title: Tag
types.description: What items belong with, named in a word or two: an item is tagged with any number of them (tagged), and a lens's filter selects by it (tagged <tag>).

types.title: Event
types.description: Something that happens at a time: a deadline, a launch, an appointment.

types.title: Resource
types.description: Something limited or exclusive that work needs: a machine, a licence, a budget, a live app.

exclusive.description: If true, only one holder at a time; everything else that needs it is blocked.

types.title: Canvas
types.description: A view kept on the map: a flat lens (a filter, a walk and a limit, as query flat takes them) and a style, so a person opens it anywhere and it draws the same. About a project or item (an about link), it is a view of that thing; about nothing, the workspace's. Its pins are drawn with what its filter finds; where things sit on it is kept in the places stream under its id, apart from the map's. Home lists them; a document line holding its id draws it there; report show with its id opens one.

filter.description: What it finds: { text, types, ids, links, exclude }, as query flat's filter. It must include something.

walk.description: From what the filter finds, along these links either way: { over: a list of link types or "all", steps }.

style.description: How it is drawn: { shape, lit, style } (a built-in drawing, what stays lit, a style kept on the map by its id).

pins.description: Items kept on it by hand, as a list of ids: drawn with what the filter finds.

pinned.description: Kept in sight by the owner: first on Home.

place.description: Its order among the views of the item it is about: the lowest first.

steps.description: How the picture came to be, step by step, ending on the map as it is: a list of steps, each changing the one before from nothing. add and remove (lists of ids), titles and flag (by id: the title then, a word marked on it then; null takes it back), fields (by id, then by name), chapter (name, when, count: the chapter this step starts) and lines (by and text: what was said). The last step is the map as it is, whatever the steps say. What a step names is sent with the picture even when finished. A drawing that knows steps plays them; others draw the map as it is.

types.title: Style
types.description: How a picture of the map is drawn, and how a page looks. About a project or item, it is how that thing's picture looks; on kinds or types (on), how every such item's pictures and pages look; about nothing, the workspace's. A field left empty comes from the level below: the workspace's, then a kind's, then the item's, then the view's. The defaults are styles too: a pack ships them as presets, and one kept on the map with the preset's id (preset) is the owner's version of it, its fields over the preset's; retired, the preset is not used. Read only by the page that draws.

shape.description: One of the drawings that come built in, used when the style has no code of its own. architecture: a system read from the top down, each part a box (a store a cylinder, a client a pill) inside a box for the place it is part of (a host, a cloud), wires at right angles from a part to what it depends on or calls, each labelled with what the link says; a dot for each part's health (read from its status: up, degraded, down, being wired, planned), and each wire wired, not yet wired (dashed) or broken (red), by the link's own state or else by its two ends. list: a table, one line a row, its marks in columns; a thing that holds others a group that folds. grid: rows by what the start holds, columns by the lens's lanes, each thing a card; no lines are drawn. time: along a time axis (the lens's time), as a calendar of days with hours down (layout: calendar) or as bars across days (layout: bars, a Gantt chart), each lane a row; the one a lens on a time axis is drawn in unless said. flow: a flat graph read from the top down, each item a step showing its name (work a box, a question a diamond, an occurrence a pill, a record a sheet), wires at right angles from what is depended on to what depends on it, every other link (part_of first) a quiet straight tie that keeps its ends near, nothing nested, an open question's choices as dashed scenarios. Any other look is code of its own. list unless said.

lit.description: What stays lit as it opens.

undrawn.description: The link types drawn as no wire, as a list, e.g. ["tagged"]: the items are still drawn and still filtered by them. An empty list draws every link the drawing draws.

layout.description: time: a calendar of days, hours running down (calendar), or each lane a row of bars across the days (bars, a Gantt chart). calendar unless said.

hours.description: time, calendar: the hours of the day shown, as [from, to], e.g. [6, 22]. The whole day unless said.

open.description: list: how many levels are open as it first draws.

show.description: list: the columns each row has, as a list of: type, status, waits, sessions. status, waits and sessions unless said.

column.description: The least width of a box, in pixels.

text.description: The size of names, in pixels.

radius.description: How round corners are, in pixels.

gap.description: The room between things, in pixels.

colors.description: Colours by name, each a hex colour: sea, land, inner, line, text, muted, blocked, you, session, done.

color_by.description: grid: the shown field each card is coloured by, e.g. kind.

rows.description: grid: what the rows are. Left empty, what the start holds. link:<kind>, the things those links lead to, e.g. link:funding.could_fund: a thing is a card in each row its links lead to, with the link's words as its second line.

palette.description: grid: a hex colour for each value of color_by, e.g. {"grant": "#2e7d4f"}. A value not named takes one of the built-in colours.

labels.description: grid: what a lane or a value is called, e.g. {"set_up": "Set up"}. Not named, it is the value in words.

detail.description: grid: the shown field written on each card's second line, e.g. amount.

mark.description: grid: the shown date field marked on a card, with the field <name>_note before it when there is one, e.g. deadline.

sizes.description: Lengths a drawing is laid out by, each by name: a number of pixels, or a length with its unit ("11ch", "68vh"). The stylesheet reads each as --ln-<name> (an underscore a dash), the drawing's code by name, e.g. flow_layer_gap. The house style names every one a built-in drawing uses.

numbers.description: Numbers a drawing is drawn by that are not lengths, each by name: how faint what is not lit is (dim), how many make a checklist (flow_fold_at), how far a step of the wheel zooms. Read as --ln-<name> too.

hues.description: The colours things are told apart by, in order, as hex colours: a grid's values with no colour of their own in palette, and a calendar's streams.

page.description: What an item's page shows, and how: picture (true to draw what it holds and is tied to above its note), notes (folded: a note opens on its first paragraph with each section a click away; whole: read through, every section open, as a document is), ties and history (open or closed as the page opens), head (invoice: a document read whole opens on its number, dates and what is due, from the fields its type shows). A preset on a kind or type says it for every such item.

theme.description: The page's colours, as light and dark, each a set of hex colours by name: bg, panel, line, text, muted, accent, ok, warn, bad, closed (each with a _soft), the kinds' g_*, edge, on_mark (words on a coloured mark), figure (behind a picture), and the reader's and the public page's (reader_*, public_*). Read as --<name>, an underscore a dash. The house style names every one.

font.description: The typeface names are written in, as CSS font-family.

dots.description: What a part's dot says, where a drawing reads it (architecture): field (the shown field it is coloured by, e.g. layer, in place of its health), colours (for each value, the name of one of the page's colours, e.g. {"kernel": "g_system"}) names (what each value is called in the key) and order (the values in the order the key gives them). Under the name of a look a story is drawn in (islands), the same again for that look: a field of status colours by the status, and the last value in order is done.

page_css.description: How a published page looks, as CSS read after the page's own (ui/doc.css, ui/doc-lens.css): rules such as h2 { ... } or section:has(> .doc-lens.wide) > h2 { ... }, read only inside the published page. Checked as a drawing's stylesheet is: no url(), no @import, no quotes or backslashes. Taken from the workspace's style when a page is opened, so a page shows a change once it is opened again (or at once, opened with ?live, when it is published again). Written by an agent, it waits for the human unless the owner lets agents change drawings (agent_code).

code.description: The drawing itself, as a JavaScript module: export default function draw({ canvas, answer, style, theme, size, tree, three, on, open, tip, cursor }). It runs in the browser of whoever looks, in a worker inside a sandboxed frame: it has a canvas to draw on and no page, no network and no storage. Written by an agent, it waits for the human to approve it before it runs. canvas is an OffscreenCanvas (2D or WebGL); answer is what the lens view answered; style is this style's other fields; theme is the page's colours (sea, land, inner, line, text, muted, blocked, you, session, done) and dark; size is { width, height, dpr }, kept current; tree() gives the answer as a tree ({ root, byId, me }, each thing with kids, up, depth and its counts all, work, blk, you, at); three() resolves to three.js; on(name, fn) hears pointerdown, pointermove, pointerup, pointerleave, wheel (each { x, y, button, buttons, deltaY, shift, ctrl }) and resize; open(id) opens an item's page; tip(text, x, y) shows words by the pointer (null hides them); cursor(name) sets the pointer. With code, shape is not used.

modules.description: The owner's version of a drawing a pack ships (with preset, the drawing's id): its modules by name, each a JavaScript module's text, standing in for the pack's module of that name. The drawing runs as code does, in a worker inside a sandboxed frame, and answers with marks (SVG and HTML as data) the page checks before it draws them. Written by an agent, it waits for the human to approve it.

on.description: The kinds or types whose pictures and pages it is for, as a list. Left empty, it is about what it is linked to by about, or the whole workspace.

preset.description: The id of the pack's style this is the owner's version of.

types.title: Screen
types.description: A page the kernel draws as one column of pieces: a picture (a lens in a style), rows from a pack's view, an action's form, an item's fields, a short note. On kinds or types (on), it is shown on the page of every such item; given a place in the nav (nav), it is a page of its own there; on Home (home), it is drawn there after the screens before it. A pack ships screens as presets; one kept on the map with the preset's id (preset) is the owner's version of it, and retired, the preset is not shown. Only a person changes a screen: an agent's change waits for them.

pieces.description: The column, in order: each {piece, ...what it needs}. picture: lens (a kept view's id, or a flat lens { filter, walk, limit }, "{here}" in its ids or link terms the item the page is of), only (the types it draws of what that finds) and style (a style's id, or its fields, code aside); view: view (a pack's view of rows) and item (the input the item's id goes in); action: action (a pack's action); fields: fields (a list of the item's fields); note: text. Left empty, the preset's.

on.description: The kinds or types on whose page it is shown, as a list. Left empty, the preset's.

nav.description: Its place in the nav, after Home and Search: the lowest first. Left empty, it is not in the nav.

home.description: Drawn on Home (true) or taken off it (false). Left empty, the preset's: a pack's screen for Home is on it.

preset.description: The id of the pack's screen this is the owner's version of.

links.title: depends on
links.description: The source cannot finish until the target is closed. Drives the blockers view.

links.title: waits on
links.description: The source cannot move until this actor (a person, a company, an agent) has answered or acted. Say what is awaited in the relation's props.for, as what they are to do, in a few words, said to them: "Choose the pack's name", not "choosing the name". Drives the blockers view; remove the link once they have.

links.title: ships
links.description: What the event brings out: open work under it that neither it waits for nor it goes ahead without is left to sort. Drives the gate view.

links.title: goes ahead without
links.description: The event was planned with this in sight and does not wait for it: it can follow. What the event does wait for is depends_on. Drives the gate view.

links.title: is part of
links.description: Hierarchy: a task in a project, a project in an area.

links.title: works at
links.description: Put the job title in the relation's props.role.

links.title: is about
links.description: A note, file, decision or issue concerns the target.

links.title: needs
links.description: The work cannot run without this place, one with a capacity (a resource). Drives the blockers view.

links.title: holds
links.description: Current occupancy of a place with a capacity (a resource). Created by claim, ended by release.

links.title: produced
links.description: The work led to this result, file or decision.

links.title: lives in
links.description: Where something is: work in a repository, a visit at a site.

links.title: bears on
links.description: Evidence on a question: a result, a test or a finding that helps settle it.

links.title: relates to
links.description: A loose link. Prefer a specific relation when one fits.

links.title: is tagged
links.description: What the item belongs with: any number of tags to an item. A lens's filter selects by it (tagged <tag id or name>); the house style draws no wire for it (undrawn).

rules.say: Code that runs in the browser of whoever looks is the human's to allow.
What a screen shows, and where, is the human's to change.
Folding one style into another can bring its code along: the human's to allow.
What anyone can see is the human's to decide.
Its pack is gone, and its rules with it: a person looks at what is written to it.
The {pack} pack touched "{title}", a {type} it neither declares nor requires.
Settling "{title}" is the owner's: the agent proposes the answer, and they confirm it.
"{title}": to settle a decision, say what was chosen (props.outcome) and why (props.rationale).
"{title}": to settle a question, say on whose authority (authority.of: "human" with where they said so, or "agent" for your own judgment).
Forgetting "{title}" is the owner's: it is for good, and cannot be undone.
The agent asked for a look before it takes effect.
This agent's token may only propose.
An agent's change waits for a person until the owner lets agents' changes apply.
Publishing is the owner’s here: they allow agents on the Workspace page, under Publishing. Ask them with publish_ask.
Agents may not download this workspace’s backups: the owner allows it on the Workspace page, under Backups.
A run's story and spend now, two weeks of how they got there, kept half a year after the run ends.
Who holds what now, a month of who held it, a claim kept three months after its release.
Who may read a notification, kept a month after it is read and three months unread.
When an automation last ran and what came of it, a week of it before.
The workspace's settings now, and a year of how they were.
When a token was last used and backups downloaded, a year of it.
A test's picture as it last ran.
The latest reading, one an hour after a day, one a day after a month.
Where each thing stands on each canvas now, and not where it stood before.
What a pack keeps, as it last kept it.

views.description: The lens: a filter, a walk and a limit, answered as items and the links among them. What the filter includes picks the seeds, any item any term finds: text (the search read's own: words in any form in titles and notes, or as typed in a title, else titles nearly what was typed; the best match first, and matched says how many it found in all), types (the newest of each, flavours included), ids, and links ("tagged e_x", "waits_on me", "part_of e_y": what has that link to it; or { link, from } for what an item links to). What it excludes (closed, system, or a type) is left out of everything, what the walk reaches included, and the walk does not pass through it; system unless exclude is given. The walk follows the link types named (over, or "all"), either way, for steps steps (1 when over is named; at most 6). The limit is the most items sent (500; at most 2000), seeds first, and cut says it cut. A filter that includes nothing is refused. Each item is its head (id, kind, type, title, the start of its note, visibility, status, open, owner, times) and the fields its type marks shown; each link its id, type, from, to and props. Params: filter ({ text, types, ids, links, exclude }), walk ({ over, steps }), limit.

What deserves attention, and why: each item with its reasons, the strongest first. Reasons: waits_on (someone must answer or act), to_confirm (an agent settled it and the owner has not confirmed), holding_up (others are blocked by it), due (its bound is near or past), unsettled (a question not yet settled, and how it settles), blocked (and what has to move first), stale (nobody has changed or confirmed it for stale_days), under_way (a session is on it), ready (work nothing blocks). Each item says what it sits in at the top (top). Params: person ("me", or an id: only what is theirs), within (an item or place: only what is its): one of the two, since weighing every open item would read the whole map (for everyone, only to_confirm), reasons (some of the above), days (due within, 7), stale_days (14), order (latest: what changed most recently first), limit (100). With to_confirm, the answer has to_confirm.upto for the confirmed tool.

Nodes and edges for drawing the map. Params: `relations` (blocking, structure or all), focus (an item id: show only its neighbourhood; without one, the newest links of each kind), depth (1 to 4, with focus), include_closed, include_system.

A tree a pack declares over "is part of", such as software.roadmap: one root and its branches in order, the work under each, progress rolled up, and what is being worked on now. Params: root (an item id; without it, the roots to choose from), tree (needed only when packs declare more than one).

The hubs within an item or a place (within, needed): open items in it that hold enough to need views of their own, largest first, each with how much it holds (inside), the size at which an item there counts as a hub (at) and how many views it has. An item is a hub when it holds at least its project's hub_at open things (12 when the project does not say; a project still being shaped sets it to 1, so that nearly everything in it is one). A hub with no views is work owed: give it its views with lens items about it. Nothing is stored: this is read off the map each time.
Everything a session needs to start on one task: context, repository, blockers, resources it needs, and the rules that apply. Params: task (required).

actions.title: Capture
actions.description: Put something on the map: an item and its links, or a record of what happened.

actions.title: Assign
actions.description: Give work to someone, inside the map or outside it: an owner, a person waited on, a party asked to act.

actions.title: Report
actions.description: Say that something happened or is so: progress, a result, a payment received, a check that it is still true.

actions.title: Ask
actions.description: Put a question to someone and wait for the answer.

actions.title: Settle
actions.description: Close a question by someone's word or by evidence: a decision made, a hypothesis borne out.

actions.title: Revise
actions.description: Change, correct or undo what is on the map.
